About the direction the brass is going... It is going outward (and often forward) because upon the introduction of the A2 upper receivers, there's a lump called the 'brass deflector' designed to keep shooters firing alongside each other from being hit with hot shell casings. Also note that sometimes the exact direction the ejected brass changes a bit, probably due to the rearward speed of the bolt increasing as it heats up. Things move faster when the lubricants come up to temp... then later they slow again, due to the crud that builds up. The ejector and spring are both carried inside the bolt, so the speed of the bolt's rearward stroke can greatly affect the force that the extractor can exert at that moment.
